commands.review_summary:
The branch clamps optional Gateway server-method model-catalog timeout overrides with the shared timer-safe resolver and adds a regression test for oversized overrides.

PR surface: Source +5, Tests +41. Total +46 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source and dependency level: current main passes a raw oversized timeout into setTimeout, and Node v24.18.0 coerces Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER to a 1ms timer. I did not run a full Gateway current-main repro, so this is source-reproducible rather than end-to-end reproduced.

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve optional catalog timeout when override is oversized
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an oversized optional model catalog timeout override could be passed through to Node timers and overflow into a near-immediate timeout instead of preserving the intended slow-catalog fallback window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional catalog path accepts timeout overrides for server-method metadata loading. Those values need to follow the same timer-safe bounds as other gateway timers so huge numeric inputs do not become `1ms` timers under Node.

## User Impact

Gateway session and agent-list responses keep their primary response path non-blocking while avoiding accidental immediate fallback behavior when an override is larger than Node's timer range.

## Evidence

- Current head: `ea94f355c8bbe8ac4fca2c85f92e9aaa2ab690db`, after merge with `upstream/main` at `b8cdb93f6ffa46f689a9ed799d9543e38228bd44`.
- Current-head focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/optional-model-catalog.test.ts` passed with `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 2 passed (2)`, and `[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 39.13s`.
- Current-head diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Local Windows runtime proof at `ea94f355c8bbe8ac4fca2c85f92e9aaa2ab690db`: a Node runtime probe called `loadOptionalServerMethodModelCatalog(..., { timeoutMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER })`, recorded the actual fallback `setTimeout` delay, shortened only the probe timer execution so the command could complete, and observed this redacted result:

```json
{
  "platform": "win32",
  "inputTimeoutMs": 9007199254740991,
  "expectedTimerDelayMs": 2147000000,
  "observedTimerDelayMs": 2147000000,
  "fallbackReturnedUndefined": true,
  "overflowWouldBeOneMsWithoutClamp": true,
  "debugLogs": [
    "agents.list continuing without model catalog after 2147000000ms"
  ]
}
```

- Observed result: the runtime scheduled the fallback at `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS` (`2147000000`) rather than allowing Node's oversized timer overflow path.
